items.followUp: Give two reasons why viruses are considered to lie at the boundary between living and non-living things.

rubric.why: The five-kingdom system classifies cellular organisms, whereas viruses lack cellular organization.
rubric.description: States that viruses lack cells or cellular structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying viruses as acellular or stating that they lack cellular structure.

rubric.why: Viruses do not carry out metabolism or other life activities independently.
rubric.description: States that viruses lack independent metabolism or life activities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the absence of independent metabolism or life activities.

rubric.why: Viruses depend on living host cells to reproduce.
rubric.description: Explains that viruses reproduce only inside living host cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that viral reproduction requires a living host cell.

rubric.why: Outside a host, viruses are inert and can be crystallized, showing why they are not included among the five kingdoms.
rubric.description: Mentions that viruses are inert outside a host or can be crystallized.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing either characteristic.

modelAnswer: Viruses are acellular and have no cellular structure.
They lack independent metabolism and other life activities.
They reproduce only inside living host cells.
Outside a host, they are inert and can be crystallized; therefore, they are not placed in any of the five kingdoms.
